clue.text: Drink merrily on large merry-go-round

parts.note: to carouse is to drink and make merry
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone drinking happily while riding a fairground ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousel is the fairground roundabout with rising and falling horses, the same ride as a merry-go-round.

clue.text: Unborn creature's enemy with time to go to America

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
T is the standard abbreviation for time
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: An unborn being's adversary heads off to the States, given time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'to go to' just place each piece after the one before.
explanation.definitionFit: A foetus is an offspring still developing in the womb, a creature not yet born.

clue.text: Let Basil out of prison

indicators.note: letting someone out sets them loose, so these letters are freed from their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A plea to release a man named Basil from jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of prison' reads as one phrase, but 'out' is the anagram signal and 'prison' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress used as a state jail, stormed in 1789 at the start of the French Revolution.

clue.text: Pleased to get rid of date unexpectedly, having forty winks

indicators.note: something unexpected comes out in a surprising order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
getting rid of something means a letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: Someone happily cancels a date and takes a nap instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove D from PLEASED, then rearrange PLEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Forty winks is a short nap, so someone having forty winks is sleeping.

clue.text: Carbon fibre pencil

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
rayon is a synthetic textile fibre

explanation.surface: A pencil made with carbon fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayon is a stick of coloured wax or chalk used like a pencil for drawing.

clue.text: Plant drug on mistress

parts.note: C is slang shorthand for cocaine
a mistress is a lover

explanation.surface: Someone hides drugs on a mistress, as if framing her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant drug on' looks like framing someone, but 'Plant' is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Clover is a low-growing herb of the pea family with three-lobed leaves.

clue.text: Sauce for animal to drink

parts.note: a cat is an animal
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A dish of sauce set out for a pet to lap up.
explanation.definitionFit: Catsup is an American variant spelling of ketchup, the tomato condiment.

clue.text: American writer to have a go at work that rhymes?

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American author
to try is to have a go

explanation.surface: An American author attempting some writing in rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that not all poetry rhymes; this is a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry is literary composition in verse, often though not always written with rhyme.

clue.text: Surgeons aim to cut up foolish people

indicators.note: cutting something up chops it into bits that can be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Surgeons intend to operate on some stupid patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut up' fits surgeons perfectly, which hides its role as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoramuses are ignorant or stupid people, the plural of ignoramus.

clue.text: Fail to take responsibility when police officer's elsewhere

parts.note: a cop is a police officer; the 's stands for 'is'
someone out is not here but elsewhere

explanation.surface: Someone shirks duty while the officer is away.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop out is an informal idiom for dodging a duty or commitment.

clue.text: Got the grade, somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unknown way, so the letters come out in an unknown order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A student surprised to have achieved the required mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got the grade' reads as one phrase; 'Got' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gathered can mean collected or acquired, the same sense as obtained.

clue.text: That man leading Schutzstaffel?

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so one part is placed before the other

parts.note: he is the pronoun for that man
SS is the abbreviation of Schutzstaffel, the Nazi paramilitary force

explanation.surface: A question about who commanded Hitler's elite guard.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a loose definition: Rudolf Hess was a senior Nazi, though Himmler, not he, led the SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Hess was Hitler's deputy in the Nazi party, a prominent figure of that regime.

clue.text: One stopping the pleasure of others from ill-gotten gains reaching harbour

definitions.text: One stopping the pleasure of others

indicators.note: reaching means arriving at, so one part runs straight on into the next

parts.note: spoils are goods taken by plunder
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: Pirates' loot arriving at a harbour, spoiling the fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilsport is a person who ruins other people's enjoyment.

clue.text: Royal house arranged Lent pageant

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A royal household organises a procession for Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plantagenets were the dynasty that ruled England from Henry II to Richard III.

clue.text: Fruit containing sadly inert source of goodness

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one part sits within the other

parts.note: a nut is a dry fruit

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fruit holding some unhappily inactive substance that is good for you.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrient is a substance that nourishes the body, a source of the goodness in food.

clue.text: Transport door

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to carry away with delight, stressed on the second syllable
second meaning: a way in, stressed on the first syllable

explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport door' suggests a vehicle's door; transport here is the verb meaning to delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance is to enrapture, and an entrance is a doorway into a building.

clue.text: King taken in by devil's associate

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being held inside it

parts.note: a fiend is a devil
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch fooled by the devil's accomplice.
explanation.definitionFit: A friend is a companion or close associate.

clue.text: Indifference to a way to capture heart of royal

indicators.note: capturing something means taking it on, so the way gains another letter at its end

parts.note: taken as written
a path is a way

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only its middle letter is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of the five-letter word

explanation.surface: Someone is unmoved by a plan to seize a royal's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Despite 'capture', nothing goes inside anything: the middle letter is simply added after A PATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is a lack of interest or concern, the same as indifference.

clue.text: Device for extracting milk from swelling containing freshly expressed repast

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one part goes within the other

parts.note: a bump is a swelling

indicators.note: expressed afresh means put a new way, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A nursing mother's gadget drawing out milk for a baby's meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressed' is apt, since expressing milk is drawing it from the breast.
explanation.definitionFit: A breast pump is a device nursing mothers use to draw milk from the breast.

clue.text: Reluctant to accept part of 7?

wordplay.note: a verse is one section of a poem, and 7 is poetry

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to take on a piece of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 refers to the answer of 7-down. The cross-reference is split as 'a verse', a stanza of poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Averse to something means opposed to it, unwilling to take it on.

clue.text: Drink finished before setter's given glass at last!

parts.note: something finished is past
the setter refers to themself as I

indicators.note: at last points to the very end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: The setter finally gets a glass once the drink is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastis is an aniseed-flavoured French aperitif, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Printing error in nasty polemic

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: letters running across the word break

explanation.surface: A misprint turns up in an unpleasant political tract.
explanation.definitionFit: A typo is a typographical slip, a mistake in printed or typed text.

clue.text: Cast net to European before fire breaks out in island

indicators.note: to cast is to throw, and thrown letters land in a new order
breaking out means bursting loose, so these letters scatter and regroup

parts.note: the letters of this word, rearranged
E is the abbreviation for European
the letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: Fishermen cast nets while a wildfire breaks out on a holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: one of the three-letter word and one of the four-letter word, with E between.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenerife is the largest of Spain's Canary Islands, off north-west Africa.

clue.text: Quick look at spineless Tory is insufficient

parts.note: a scan is a quick look

indicators.note: without a spine means the middle is removed, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A glance at a weak-willed Conservative shows he falls short.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty means meagre, too small in amount to be enough.

clue.text: Giving medication to scoundrel admitting lust, say

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: dog is an old word for a rogue or scoundrel
lust is one of the seven deadly sins; 'say' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A doctor treats a rogue who confesses to lust.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosing is administering doses of a medicine to someone.

clue.text: Irritation in empty tummy is not very significant

indicators.note: in places one part inside the other
emptying a word removes its inside, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
an itch is an irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: An itch in a hungry stomach is only a minor matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Titchy is British slang for very small.
explanation.definitionFit: Titchy is informal British for tiny, so of little size or importance.
